items.description: Repository structure analysis and module inventory
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/module_inventory.md documenting every module in .archivara/ (concept_evolve.py, semantic_scholar.py, opencode.json), .opencode/ (agents/, tools/, package.json), results/, and figures/. For each module: (a) file path, (b) language, (c) line count, (d) one-sentence purpose, (e) upstream/downstream dependencies within the repo. Must cover at least 10 distinct files. Include a dependency diagram in Mermaid syntax.

items.description: Web-based literature review on parallel and high-performance DEFLATE decompression
items.acceptance_criteria: Use websearch tool with at least 15 distinct queries spanning: (1) parallel DEFLATE/gzip decompression, (2) speculative decompression, (3) SIMD-accelerated Huffman decoding, (4) GPU decompression (GDeflate, nvcomp), (5) hardware decompression accelerators, (6) cache-aware streaming decompression, (7) branch-free entropy decoding. Produce results/phase1/literature_review.md with structured summaries of at least 15 distinct works. Each summary must include: title, authors/organization, year, venue/source, key contribution (2-3 sentences), relevance to our 2-5x speedup goal, and identified limitations. Subagent delegation: use literature-graph-miner agent to mine citation graphs starting from pugz, libdeflate, and GDeflate seed papers.
items.notes: This is the foundational literature item. All later phases reference it.

items.description: Build citation graph and create sources.bib with BibTeX entries
items.acceptance_criteria: Use semantic_scholar tool (graph command) with seed queries: 'parallel DEFLATE decompression', 'speculative gzip parallelism', 'SIMD Huffman decoding', 'GPU lossless decompression'. Create sources.bib in repo root with valid BibTeX entries for at least 10 relevant papers. Each entry must have: author, title, year, venue/journal fields. Save citation graph JSON to results/phase1/citation_graph.json with at least 25 nodes and connecting edges. Cross-reference entries against results/phase1/literature_review.md to ensure consistency.

items.description: RFC 1951 DEFLATE specification analysis for exploitable parallelism properties
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/deflate_spec_analysis.md containing: (a) enumeration of DEFLATE block types (00, 01, 10, 11) with bit-level format diagrams, (b) Huffman code structure constraints (max 15-bit codes, code-length alphabet), (c) LZ77 window constraint (32KB) and implications for parallel decomposition, (d) at least 5 structural properties exploitable for parallelism (e.g., block-local Huffman tables, bounded back-reference distance, deterministic end-of-block symbols, stored-block alignment, dynamic-table prefix codes), (e) comparison of gzip framing (RFC 1952) vs raw DEFLATE vs ZIP entry framing for parallel entry-point discovery. Must cite RFC 1951 and RFC 1952 in sources.bib.

items.description: Survey existing high-performance DEFLATE implementations with optimization technique catalog
items.acceptance_criteria: Search the web for source repositories and benchmarks of: libdeflate, zlib-ng, Intel ISA-L, CloudFlare zlib, Chromium zlib, pigz, pugz, GDeflate/nvcomp, zstd (for comparison), and at least 2 additional implementations. Produce results/phase1/implementation_survey.md with for each: (a) repository URL, (b) language/platform, (c) key optimization techniques (SIMD intrinsics, multi-threading model, lookup-table design, memory-mapping), (d) published benchmark numbers with hardware context, (e) license. Add all implementations as @misc BibTeX entries to sources.bib. Total sources.bib entries must be at least 15 after this item.

items.description: Concept-tree evolution on DEFLATE decompression bottlenecks with cross-domain exploration
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve 'evolve' command on topic 'parallel DEFLATE decompression bottlenecks and cross-domain acceleration techniques'. Resulting results/concept_evolve/tree/ must contain: (a) at least 10 concept card folders each with concept.json and README.md, (b) index.json indexing all cards, (c) results/concept_evolve/semantic_bridge.json with at least 15 edges connecting concepts across domains, (d) results/concept_evolve/tree/walk_paths.json with at least 5 traversal paths of depth >= 3. Produce results/phase1/sub_problems.md documenting exactly 5 decomposed sub-problems: (1) block boundary detection, (2) Huffman table reconstruction at arbitrary offsets, (3) LZ77 back-reference resolution across speculative boundaries, (4) work partitioning and load balancing, (5) correctness verification and fixup. Subagent delegation: use concept-tree-explorer agent to identify the 3 highest-value concept paths after evolve completes.

items.description: Assemble diverse DEFLATE test corpus with structural characterization
items.acceptance_criteria: Create data/ directory with at least 5 test files: (a) highly compressible text (>=100MB uncompressed, e.g., enwik8), (b) mixed-type ZIP archive (>=100MB, text + binary + images), (c) poorly compressible binary (>=50MB, near-random data), (d) small-file ZIP (>=1000 entries, >=50MB total), (e) single large gzip stream (>=200MB uncompressed). Record in results/phase2/corpus_metadata.json: filename, format, compressed_size_bytes, uncompressed_size_bytes, compression_ratio, estimated_deflate_block_count for each file.

items.description: Build libdeflate and establish single-threaded decompression baseline
items.acceptance_criteria: Clone and build libdeflate (latest release) in vendor/libdeflate/. Write benchmarks/bench_libdeflate.c that decompresses each corpus file 10 times, measuring: (a) wall-clock time (median, p5, p95), (b) throughput in GB/s for both compressed input and uncompressed output, (c) CPU cycles via rdtsc or perf_event. Results saved to results/phase2/baseline_libdeflate.json. Throughput measurements must be reproducible within 5% variance across runs.

items.description: Benchmark additional baselines (zlib-ng, ISA-L, pigz) and produce ranked comparison
items.acceptance_criteria: Build zlib-ng and Intel ISA-L in vendor/. Write benchmarks/bench_baselines.sh that measures decompression throughput for zlib-ng, ISA-L igzip, pigz -d, and system unzip/gunzip on all corpus files. Results saved to results/phase2/baseline_all.json with same schema as item_008. Produce results/phase2/baseline_comparison.md with a ranked table of all implementations by uncompressed-output throughput (GB/s) on each corpus file. Identify the current fastest single-threaded and multi-threaded implementations. Subagent delegation: use general agent to build all vendor libraries in parallel.

items.description: Profile decompression bottlenecks with hardware performance counters
items.acceptance_criteria: Run perf record + perf report (or equivalent profiling) on libdeflate decompressing the largest corpus file. Produce results/phase2/bottleneck_profile.md documenting: (a) top 10 hotspot functions with % of total cycles, (b) IPC (instructions per cycle), (c) branch misprediction rate, (d) L1/L2/L3 cache miss rates, (e) clear identification of whether primary bottleneck is Huffman decoding (instruction-bound), LZ77 copy (memory-bound), or I/O. Raw perf data saved to results/phase2/perf_data.txt.

items.description: Characterize DEFLATE stream structure and define target performance metrics
items.acceptance_criteria: Write src/tools/block_scanner.py (or .c) that parses DEFLATE streams outputting: block count, block-type distribution, average/median/max block sizes (compressed and uncompressed), Huffman table diversity (unique tables count), back-reference distance histogram (buckets: 0-256, 256-4K, 4K-32K). Run on all corpus files. Save to results/phase2/stream_structure.json. Define target metrics in results/phase2/target_metrics.md: primary = aggregate decompression throughput (GB/s uncompressed), target >= 3x fastest single-threaded baseline; secondary = parallel efficiency (speedup/thread_count), memory overhead ratio (peak_RSS/uncompressed_size), latency to first decompressed byte.

items.description: Implement speculative multi-entry-point intra-stream parallel DEFLATE decompression
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/speculative_decompress.c (or .rs): (a) divide a single DEFLATE stream at N evenly-spaced byte offsets, (b) at each offset, scan forward (up to 64KB) to locate a valid Huffman block boundary via heuristic bit-pattern validation, (c) speculatively decompress each segment independently into thread-local buffers, (d) sequential merge pass resolving cross-boundary LZ77 back-references by copying from the preceding segment's output tail (up to 32KB). Must compile without errors and produce byte-exact output matching libdeflate on at least 3 corpus files. Code comments must cite pugz (Lecompte et al.) and any other relevant entries from sources.bib. Unit tests in tests/test_speculative.c.
items.notes: Core novel contribution. Depends on items 004, 006 for sub-problem decomposition and item 010 for bottleneck understanding.

items.description: Implement ZIP-level file-parallel decompression with work-stealing scheduler
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/zip_parallel.c (or .rs): (a) parse ZIP central directory to enumerate entries, (b) dispatch member decompression to a work-stealing thread pool, (c) use mmap or pread for contention-free concurrent I/O, (d) handle both stored and DEFLATE-compressed entries. Byte-exact output verified against reference unzip on the small-files corpus. Measure speedup vs single-threaded libdeflate on corpus item (d) from item_007.

items.description: Implement hybrid two-level parallelism combining file-parallel and intra-stream speculation
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/hybrid_decompress.c (or .rs): (a) outer level dispatches ZIP members or gzip files to threads, (b) inner level applies speculative intra-stream decomposition (item_012) for members exceeding 1MB threshold, (c) adaptive thread allocation between outer and inner levels. Unit tests pass on all corpus files. Produce results/phase3/amdahl_analysis.md with theoretical maximum speedup estimates per corpus file given measured sequential fractions.

items.description: SIMD-accelerated block boundary detection and Huffman decoding acceleration
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in src/simd_accel.c (or .rs): (a) SSE4.2/AVX2 routine scanning byte buffers for candidate DEFLATE block boundaries by testing BFINAL/BTYPE patterns at all bit offsets within SIMD lanes, (b) lightweight Huffman header validation filter to prune false positives, (c) scalar fallback for non-SIMD platforms. Standalone boundary scanner must process >= 4 GB/s of compressed input on the largest corpus file. Integrate into item_012's entry-point discovery. Benchmark results in results/phase3/simd_scan_bench.json comparing SIMD vs scalar scan throughput.

items.description: Concept-tree blind-spot exploration for overlooked acceleration opportunities
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve 'probe' on 'DEFLATE decompression performance blind spots' and 'reframe' on 'faster-than-memory decompression'. In results/concept_evolve/tree/, at least 3 new concept folders must be created beyond those from item_006. Produce results/phase3/blind_spots.md summarizing: (a) at least 3 novel ideas not covered by items 012-015 (candidates: entropy-based block size prediction, PEXT/PDEP branch-free Huffman, decode-table compression for L1 residency, memory-mapped page-fault-driven scheduling, CRC elision for trusted streams), (b) feasibility rating (high/medium/low) for each, (c) priority ordering. At least one idea must be selected and prototyped in Phase 4. Subagent delegation: use concept-tree-explorer to walk the expanded tree and rank paths by novelty and feasibility.

items.description: Comprehensive throughput benchmarking of all implementations across full corpus
items.acceptance_criteria: Run benchmarks/bench_all.sh measuring decompression throughput (GB/s uncompressed) for: (a) libdeflate, (b) zlib-ng, (c) ISA-L, (d) pigz -d, (e) speculative parallel (item_012), (f) ZIP-parallel (item_013), (g) hybrid (item_014), (h) hybrid+SIMD (items 014+015). Each measurement: 10 runs, report median/p5/p95. Results in results/phase4/throughput_all.json. At least one of our implementations must demonstrate >= 2x throughput over the fastest single-threaded baseline on multi-file corpus, or clearly document why not.

items.description: Thread-scaling experiment from 1 to max hardware threads
items.acceptance_criteria: For each parallel implementation (items 012, 013, 014), measure throughput at thread counts: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and max_hw_threads. On the largest single-stream corpus file and the small-files corpus. Save to results/phase4/thread_scaling.json. Produce results/phase4/thread_scaling.md with: (a) speedup curves, (b) parallel efficiency at each point, (c) bottleneck identification (Amdahl serial fraction, memory bandwidth saturation, lock contention) per implementation. Subagent delegation: use general agent to run scaling experiments across corpus files in parallel.

items.description: Speculation accuracy and recovery overhead measurement
items.acceptance_criteria: Instrument item_012's speculative decompressor to log per-run: (a) speculative entry points attempted, (b) entry points landing on valid block boundaries, (c) mean forward-scan distance to valid boundary (bytes), (d) segments requiring back-reference fixup, (e) fixup data volume (bytes). Run on all corpus files. Save to results/phase4/speculation_accuracy.json. Produce results/phase4/speculation_analysis.md interpreting: success rate vs block-size distribution (from item_011), wasted-work ratio, and whether speculation success correlates with compression ratio.

items.description: Comparison of results against prior work from literature review
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase4/literature_comparison.md containing: (a) table comparing our throughput numbers against published results for pugz, GDeflate/nvcomp, ISA-L, and at least 3 other systems from the survey (normalize by hardware generation where possible), (b) analysis of which techniques from the literature we matched/exceeded/fell short of and why, (c) at least 2 techniques from literature not yet explored in our implementation. Must reference at least 8 specific citation keys from sources.bib.

items.description: Ablation study isolating contribution of each optimization layer
items.acceptance_criteria: Measure throughput on the 3 largest corpus files for configurations: (a) speculative-only, (b) speculative + SIMD boundary scan, (c) ZIP-parallel-only, (d) hybrid (ZIP + speculative), (e) full system (hybrid + SIMD). Save to results/phase4/ablation.json. Produce results/phase4/ablation.md with stacked contribution analysis showing marginal throughput gain of each layer as absolute GB/s delta and percentage improvement.

items.description: Correctness verification via byte-exact comparison and fuzz testing
items.acceptance_criteria: Byte-exact comparison of our best implementation's output against libdeflate on all corpus files: zero byte differences allowed. Additionally, generate at least 100 random DEFLATE streams (varying block types, sizes, back-reference distances, compression levels) and verify decompression correctness. Save to results/phase4/correctness.json with pass/fail per test. 100% pass rate required.

items.description: Statistical analysis with confidence intervals and significance tests
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/statistical_analysis.md containing: (a) 95% confidence intervals for each throughput measurement from the 10-run data, (b) paired statistical test (Wilcoxon signed-rank or paired t-test) comparing our best implementation vs libdeflate with p < 0.05, (c) effect size (Cohen's d or rank-biserial correlation), (d) variance analysis identifying noise sources (OS scheduling, thermal throttling, DVFS). Raw computations in results/phase5/stats.json.

items.description: Generate publication-quality figures for all key results
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce at least 6 figures in figures/ (PNG or PDF, >= 300 DPI): (a) throughput bar chart across all implementations per corpus file, (b) thread-scaling speedup curves, (c) speculation accuracy scatter plot, (d) ablation waterfall chart, (e) block-size distribution histogram from stream characterization, (f) cache miss rate or IPC comparison. Each figure must have labeled axes, legend, and caption in figures/captions.md. Subagent delegation: use general agent to generate all figures in parallel from JSON result files.

items.description: Concept-tree evolution narrative and idea provenance trace
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/concept_narrative.md tracing idea evolution through results/concept_evolve/tree/: (a) which concept cards led to implemented techniques, (b) which cross-domain bridges from semantic_bridge.json produced actionable insights, (c) which blind-spot probes (item_016) yielded novel approaches, (d) ranked list of 5 most productive concept paths from walk_paths.json with explanation. Must reference at least 5 specific concept card folder names from the tree. Subagent delegation: use concept-tree-explorer agent to rank paths by outcome impact.

items.description: Limitations, threats to validity, and future work documentation
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/limitations.md with: (a) at least 5 threats to internal validity (measurement methodology, hardware specificity, compiler optimization sensitivity, corpus representativeness, thermal state), (b) at least 3 threats to external validity (generalization to ARM/Apple Silicon, HTTP streaming use case, PNG row-filter interaction, embedded systems), (c) at least 5 future work directions with feasibility estimates (GPU offload, hardware accelerator integration, compression-format co-design, adaptive speculation strategies, kernel-bypass I/O), (d) honest assessment of which conditions the 2-5x target was/was not achieved.

items.description: Reproducibility package with build instructions and automated benchmark runner
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce: (a) BUILD.md in repo root with step-by-step build instructions for Ubuntu 22.04+ from clean checkout, (b) scripts/run_all_benchmarks.sh that runs the complete benchmark suite outputting all JSON result files, (c) scripts/generate_figures.py that regenerates all figures from JSON, (d) results/phase5/reproducibility_checklist.md confirming: code compiles, tests pass, benchmarks run, figures generate, all with documented dependency versions.
